blocks.title: What do you need done?
blocks.text: Copy a prompt below into Copilot · [ask the Concierge]({Url:ConciergeUrl}) · [message us on Teams]({Url:TeamsUrl}) · [start a request]({Page:requests})
What do you want to do?

items.title: Clear my admin queue
body: Go through my unread mail from the last three days. Group it into: needs a reply from me, needs a decision, FYI only. For each one give me the sender, one line of context, and what you think I should do.

items.title: Create my morning brief
body: Look at my calendar and mail for today. Tell me what I need to prepare for, what I owe someone, and where my two free blocks are. Keep it under 150 words.

items.title: Teach my repeatable work
body: I do this task about once a week: [describe it]. Ask me whatever you need to know, then write me a prompt I can reuse every time. Tell me what information you will need each time and what you will not be able to see.

items.title: New hire
body: *I am new at {OrganizationName}. What can I use AI for, what must I never put in, and where do I go when I am unsure?*

items.title: Employee
body: *Here is something I do every week: [describe it]. Can I use AI for it, and what must I check before the output counts?*

items.title: Manager
body: *My team wants to use AI for [describe it]. What has to be true before I say yes, and what goes to the AI CoE first?*

items.label: Status
items.text: Concierge answering, {ConciergeSourceCount} sources, newest {ConciergeNewestSourceDate} so nothing more recent. Prompts: {PromptCount}, all draft. Teams pilot, leadership reporting and automated runs: none. Verified {VerifiedDate}.

items.label: Support
items.text: something wrong or contradictory? Tell the AI CoE. No PHI, customer data, credentials or regulated information unless the approved environment is confirmed. Private pilot: {PilotMembers}.

blocks.text: Four short things. None of them is reading. Each one is something you do with AI, and doing it is how you learn it.
[Ask the AI CoE]({Url:ConciergeUrl}) — opens in a new tab, takes a few seconds to load.
Every rule shown here as a pilot rule is PROPOSED pending policy-owner confirmation.

items.title: 1. Ask it something real
body: The AI CoE helps you use AI safely at {OrganizationName}. It does not approve tools, approve spending, or make legal, HR, security or compliance decisions.

**Do this**: ask the Concierge one real question from your own work this week. If it cannot answer from approved sources it will say so and tell you who owns the answer. That is the behaviour to expect, not a failure.

items.title: 2. Check before you paste
body: Never put PHI, customer data, credentials or regulated information into an unapproved workflow. Your own drafts, approved internal documents, published policy and public research are generally fine.

**Do this**: before pasting anything you are unsure about, ask Copilot: *Is there anything in this document I should not put into an AI tool? List anything that looks like personal health information, customer identifiers, credentials, or regulated data, and tell me where in the document it is.*

items.title: 3. Make a prompt better
body: Three habits: say what you want back, say what it may use, and ask it to show its uncertainty.

**Do this**: take a prompt you already use and add this line to it: *After your answer, list anything you were unsure about and what you would need in order to be sure.* Compare the two answers. That comparison is the lesson.

items.title: 4. Ask for something
body: Three routes: submit an idea, check a tool or task, or register AI you already use. Each returns a record id, an owner and a next step.
**Do this**: send one real request from the [Requests page]({Page:requests}). Not a test one.

blocks.text: How we know you have done it
There is no form and no checkbox. Filling in a form is not evidence that anyone learned anything, and nobody does it.
If you want to check your own understanding, ask the Concierge:
*Quiz me on safe AI use at {OrganizationName}. Ask me four questions one at a time, wait for my answer, then tell me what I got wrong and why. Use only approved {OrganizationName} AI CoE sources.*
That takes about three minutes and it is worth more than a completion record. If you would rather just start using it, do that instead.
If you lead a team
You do not need the four above. What you need is the operating picture: decisions waiting on you, adoption, and outcomes. Ask the AI CoE for the {LeadTeamContinuation}
Approved ways to use AI at {OrganizationName}. Every one is a prompt you can copy right now. All of them run in [Copilot Chat]({Url:CopilotChatUrl}) — no new tool, no licence, no approval.

Not sure your material is safe to paste? Run this first: *Is there anything in this document I should not put into an AI tool? List anything that looks like personal health information, customer identifiers, credentials, or regulated data, and tell me where in the document it is.* If it finds something, stop and use [Requests]({Page:requests}).
Everyday knowledge work

items.title: Summarise to decisions
body: Summarise this document in five bullets. Each bullet should be a decision or an action, not a topic. If there are no decisions in it, say so instead of padding.
items.meta: Approved internal documents. Verify each decision against the source.

items.title: Answer only from this source
body: Answer only from the document I have attached. If the answer is not in it, say not in this document rather than filling the gap from general knowledge.
items.meta: Approved internal documents. Confirm the answer appears in the source.

items.title: Prepare me for this meeting
body: Using the agenda and any prior decisions I have shared, give me a one-page brief: what this meeting must decide, what is already agreed, what is contested, and three questions I should ask.
items.meta: Agendas and approved decisions. No transcripts or recordings.

blocks.text: Owners, leaders and initiative teams

items.title: Start a business case
body: Help me build a business case for an AI idea. Ask me what you need in turn: problem, who it affects, current cost or time, proposed change, expected benefit, how we would measure it, who owns the benefit. Do not fill in any number I have not given you. Where I do not know something, mark it as pending baseline.
items.meta: Every number must be labelled actual, estimated, target or pending baseline before this goes to anyone.

items.title: Weekly closeout
body: Look at my last five working days across my mail, calendar and files. Give me five sections and nothing else: Done, Moved, Owed, Waiting on someone else, Didn't move. Use only what you can see. If you cannot tell whether something finished, put it in Moved and say why. Never guess at an outcome.
items.meta: Your own mail and calendar. Correct anything wrong before treating it as a record.

blocks.text: Policy, functional and content owners

items.title: Synthesise research with sources
body: Synthesise the sources I have given you into a short brief. For every claim, say which source it came from. Where sources disagree, say so rather than picking one. List what you could not find.
items.meta: Check every citation resolves before circulating.

items.title: Show me your uncertainty
body: After your answer, list anything you were unsure about and what you would need in order to be sure.
items.meta: Add this to any prompt whose output someone else will rely on.

blocks.text: Analysts and technical teams

items.title: Explain this spreadsheet
body: Look at this spreadsheet and tell me: what it appears to measure, which columns look calculated, anything that looks like an error or an outlier, and three questions I should ask the owner.
items.meta: Approved internal data only. No customer or patient records.

items.title: Build your own
body: I do this task about once a week: [describe it]. Ask me whatever you need to know, then write me a prompt I can reuse every time. Tell me what information you will need each time and what you will not be able to see.
items.meta: If it works, contribute it to the [Prompts library]({Page:prompts}).

blocks.text: What this page does not do

It does not approve a specific tool, dataset or workflow for you. It does not replace {OrganizationName} policy. It does not make the output correct — every prompt names a human check, and the check is the part that matters.
All prompts here are Draft — in review in the [Prompts library]({Page:prompts}). Use them on your own work. Their output is not {OrganizationName} guidance. Read back {StatusDate}.
Just ask. We will tell you which lane you are in.
You do not need to know whether something needs approval. Describe what you want to do and you get an answer in the same conversation.
[Ask the AI CoE]({Url:ConciergeUrl}) and choose **Can I just do this** | [Or message us on Teams]({Url:TeamsUrl})
The three lanes

items.title: Green — just do it
body: No approval needed. You get the prompt or the steps and you are done. **Most requests are green** and you will be told so plainly.
items.note: Nothing to submit. Nothing to wait for.

items.title: Amber — needs a person
body: PHI, customer data, credentials, regulated information, spend, new tool access, or a policy question.
The Concierge names who it goes to and writes the request for you in one block you can send.
items.note: You do not fill anything in.

items.title: Red — needs a business case
body: Worth doing, but it needs sizing before anyone commits.
The Concierge interviews you one question at a time and produces the case. It will not invent a number you have not given it.
items.note: Unknowns are marked pending baseline, not guessed.

items.title: What we do not ask you to do
body: Fill in fields we could have asked you about in conversation. Know the right category before you start. Write a business case unaided. Chase your own request. Keep a reference number to prove you asked.
If any of that happens, it is a fault in the service, not in you. Tell us.

items.title: Register AI you already use
body: No penalty, ever. Shadow use is a signal, not a discipline problem — it tells the CoE what people actually need.
Just say what you use and what for. That is the whole thing.

blocks.text: If you would rather use a form
The private-pilot intake form is still here. It is the fallback, not the front door.
Reusable starting points. A prompt here saves you writing one from scratch. It does not make the output approved — you still do the human check named on the record.
[Open the full library]({Url:PromptLibraryUrl}) — every record with its body, data boundary, human check and status.

body: **{PromptCount} records**, read back live on {StatusDate}. {PromptsAddedCount} added {PromptsAddedDate} and verified to run in Copilot Chat with Work IQ. {PromptTestRecordCount} are earlier test records, marked as such.

items.title: What Draft means
body: **Nothing here is approved yet, and no record has a reviewer.**
Draft means you may use it on your own work and judge the result yourself. It does not mean the output can be handed to someone else as {OrganizationName} guidance.
Approval needs a named reviewer and a decision. That has not happened, and saying otherwise would be inventing a status.

blocks.text: Everything on this page is what is actually true on {StatusDate}, not what is planned.

items.title: What is running
body: **Concierge** — answering, grounded in {ConciergeSourceCount} approved sources. Newest source dated {ConciergeNewestSourceDate}, so it cannot answer on anything more recent. It says when something is not established rather than guessing.
**Prompts library** — {PromptCount} records, all Draft — in review. Usable on your own work; not {OrganizationName} guidance.
**Learn** — four short exercises. No completion form.

items.title: What is not running
body: **Teams pilot** — not active. Separate approval required.
**Leadership reporting** — not established. No governed reporting view exists.
**Scheduled or automated runs** — none. Everything here is something a person runs by hand.
**Self-service status lookup** — not built.

items.title: Checking a request you sent
body: Keep the acknowledgement you received — it carries your record id. To find out where it stands, ask the AI CoE with that id, or use [Requests]({Page:requests}) and say you are following up. A person answers. There is no automated reply and no agreed response time.

items.title: If something is wrong
body: Tell the AI CoE. Wrong answers, broken links, a page that contradicts another page — all useful, none of it a complaint. This is a private pilot and finding faults is the point.
**What this page will never show:** an adoption number, a time-saved figure or a benefit claim without a measured baseline behind it. If you see one unlabelled, that is a fault worth reporting.
